# Flossie Tulk

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c30 P25](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0025)</sub>
- **Origin:** Brierley
- **Role:** Student  <sub>[v1 c30 P22](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0022)</sub>

## Appearance

Flossie is known for her red hair and a heavier build. She wears fashionable dresses decorated with flounces.

## Personality

Flossie possesses a difficult, moody, and vindictive temperament. Marked by a lack of imagination, she is widely recognized as caustic-tongued, bold, and direct in her questioning. She frequently exhibits a spiteful, mocking attitude toward peers and holds long-standing grudges over minor slights.

_Sources: [v1 c30 P31](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0031)_

## Traits

- bold
- caustic-tongued
- superstitious  <sub>[v1 c32 P7](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0007)</sub>
- vindictive
- lacking imagination
- fear of being held responsible for Nell's death

## Abilities

- accomplished handcrafter
- knitting lace

## Goals

- to gain an education without needing to earn a living  <sub>[v1 c30 P22](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0022)</sub>

## History

Flossie attended Brierley School under Miss Thorne as a member of the Regent's class. Known for her spiteful behavior toward Nell Harcourt, she giggled when Miss Thorne caught Nell reading a novel in class and openly mocked her appearance. She once dared Nell to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Pembroke's kitchen roof after walking a wooden fence herself, resulting in Nell falling and sustaining a severe injury. Flossie later traveled to the Academy to sit for the Entrance examinations alongside her peers, correctly predicting Hugh Carrow's victory and passing by a small margin. Following her studies in Brierley, she moved to the city to attend the Academy and Regent's.

_Sources: [v1 c30 P9](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0009), [v1 c30 P28](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0028), [v1 c32 P16](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0016)_

## Background by volume

- her family can afford her tuition, so she does not need to work for a living  <sub>[v1 c30 P22](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0022)</sub>
- won top prize for knitted lace at an exhibition
- lost her top rank in class after misspelling the word 'ebullition'
- refused to speak to Julia Bell for three months over a comment about her bow
- her mother's cousin in Boston is married to a man who attended school with a noted American artist
